name: Seeed reTerminal E1001 (4-level grayscale)
description: 7.5 inch monochrome ePaper terminal, ESP32-S3, battery-powered (800x480), driven in the panel's 4-gray waveform mode. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF grayscale build (seeed-reterminal-e1001-gray env) and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray2_bin produces a raw 2-bpp 4-level grayscale buffer (96000 bytes) the firmware paints without any on-device decode.
notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running the tesserae-device-firmware grayscale build. Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), row-major from top-left, 4 pixels per byte MSB first (bits 7-6 = leftmost pixel), 2-bit value 0b00 = black, 0b11 = white, linear 4-level gray; no header, no padding, no checksum. Same physical unit as `seeed_reterminal_e1001`; pick this kind when the unit runs the grayscale firmware build. The server migrates a registered E1001 to this kind automatically when its firmware re-registers or re-discovers declaring it (same-protocol kind heal).

beep_enabled.label: Beep on interaction
beep_enabled.help: Sound the on-board buzzer the moment a button press registers, before the server is contacted. E-ink takes seconds to repaint, so without it there is no confirmation the panel heard you. Off by default: a panel that starts beeping unannounced is worse than a silent one.

beep_tone.label: Beep tone
beep_tone.help: Which sound to make. The buzzer is a passive piezo, loudest around 2 kHz.

beep_volume.label: Beep volume
beep_volume.help: Drive strength as a percentage. The piezo is loudest at 100 and audible but discreet around 30; 0 is silent, same as turning the beep off.
